newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: SIMEX Brent quoted down, but sales seen limited.
newsitem.headline: SIMEX Brent quoted down, but sales seen limited.

text.p: August Brent futures were quoted to the downside on Tuesday, keeping in line with NYMEX which eased off on the back of Iraqi news.
But brokers said the Iraq news was now absorbed by the market and in the absence of fresh news, technical factors would limit the downside ahead of the API release later on Tuesday.
August Brent on SIMEX was quoted at midday at $17.65/$17.82 per barrel after London dropped 27 cents to $17.92.
NYMEX August crude in New York fell 34 cents to $18.99 and extended the fall on ACCESS by six cents to $18.93.
Both markets fell on news that Iraq was closer to resuming oil sales.

United Nations coordinator in Baghdad, Staffan de Mistura, said Monday that discussions about the Iraq aid plan had been completed and it would be submitted to the U.N. secretary general for final approval by next Monday.
Iraq has said it wanted to complete the aid distribution plan before resuming oil sales. It can sell $2 billion worth over a six-month period.
But Brent was also being depressed by Germany's plan to sell strategic reserves. Brokers said the sell off would continue to create volatility as the timing of each tranche sale becomes known.
But on the day Tuesday, the news has been factored into prices.
Tom James, Asia Pacific manager for Credit Lyonnais Rouse, said Brent and NYMEX were oversold which would limit any downside.
It was also likely to spark some short covering ahead of the release after the New York close Tuesday of the latest API data.
